subject: Microbiology & immunology
summary: Arthropod vectors are insects or arachnids that transmit viruses, bacteria, and parasites to humans. Clinicians must recognize exposure risk, early symptoms, and diagnostic clues to initiate timely treatment and prevent complications.

sections.p: Arthropod vectors such as mosquitoes, ticks, sandflies, and fleas carry diverse pathogens that cause acute febrile illnesses, neurological disease, and chronic infections. Their life cycles and feeding habits determine transmission patterns.

Vectors are ectoparasites that feed on blood, acquiring pathogens from infected hosts and later inoculating them into new hosts. Their saliva contains anticoagulants and immunomodulators that facilitate pathogen entry.
b: Life cycle includes larval and adult stages

sections.p: Transmission occurs when a vector bites a human, depositing pathogens into the bloodstream. Vector breeding sites, seasonality, and human behavior influence exposure risk.
b: Ticks require host contact for attachment

sections.p: Vector-borne pathogens cause a spectrum from self-limited febrile illness to severe neurological disease. Common presentations include fever, rash, arthralgia, and in severe cases, hemorrhage or encephalitis.

t.b: Normal platelets may still occur in early dengue
Mild elevation can be seen in many infections

sections.p: Clinical suspicion is guided by exposure history and symptom pattern. Laboratory confirmation relies on antigen detection, PCR, or serology, depending on the pathogen and timing.
b: History of travel to endemic area
Onset of fever with rash or joint pain

sections.p: Management focuses on supportive care, specific antiviral or antimicrobial therapy when available, and vector control measures. Clinicians must weigh drug toxicity and local resistance patterns.

Remember that vector-borne diseases often present with nonspecific fever; a detailed exposure history is key. Early recognition of warning signs such as bleeding, altered mental status, or shock mandates urgent care.
b: Always ask about recent travel or outdoor activities
Use RDTs when available but confirm with PCR or serology
Treat severe dengue with fluid resuscitation and monitor platelet trend

faq.q: Can a single mosquito bite cause disease?
faq.a: Yes, if the mosquito carries a pathogen, it can transmit it in one bite.

faq.q: Do all mosquitoes transmit the same viruses?
faq.a: No, different species carry specific viruses; Aedes transmits dengue, Zika, chikungunya.

faq.q: What is the best way to prevent tick bites?
faq.a: Use insect repellent, wear long sleeves, check for ticks after outdoor exposure, and remove promptly.
